title: HBURST, HSIZE, and Address Progression
description: Open a burst family or HSIZE to connect beat count, address increment, wrapping boundary, and alignment checks.

signals.name: HSIZE
signals.description: HSIZE selects the number of bytes in every beat and therefore the increment between sequential addresses.
signals.sampled: With every accepted address phase; stable for a burst
signals.typicalUse: For HSIZE=010, sequential word addresses increase by four bytes.
signals.verificationNote: HADDR must be aligned to 2^HSIZE and HSIZE cannot exceed the physical data-bus width.

signals.name: SINGLE
signals.description: A standalone transfer with one NONSEQ address phase and no continuing SEQ beats.
signals.sampled: With the single accepted address phase
signals.typicalUse: Register access or isolated memory operation
signals.verificationNote: A SEQ transfer must not follow as part of the same SINGLE burst.

signals.name: INCR
signals.description: Starts with NONSEQ and continues with any number of SEQ beats, incrementing HADDR by 2^HSIZE.
signals.typicalUse: Streaming transfers where length is controlled elsewhere
signals.verificationNote: Ensure arbitration or system policy prevents an unbounded INCR burst from starving other traffic.

signals.name: INCR4/8/16
signals.description: Transfer exactly 4, 8, or 16 beats with each address increasing by the HSIZE byte count.
signals.sampled: Stable from first NONSEQ through final SEQ beat
signals.verificationNote: Count accepted beats, not elapsed cycles; wait states do not consume beats.

signals.name: WRAP4/8/16
signals.description: Increment addresses within a boundary equal to beats × bytes-per-beat, then wrap to the bottom of that boundary.
signals.sampled: Stable from first NONSEQ through final SEQ beat
signals.typicalUse: Cache-line fills beginning at the requested critical word
signals.verificationNote: Compute the wrap boundary from both HBURST and HSIZE; common bugs wrap on the wrong byte boundary.
